Definition: properly, dyed, i.e. a turban (probably as of colored stuff)
BiblicalUsage: Ezekiel pictures the Chaldean captains with dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to. The word is a turban, dyed stuff, the coloured head-dress of officers. It appears once, in the portrait of the lovers Jerusalem lusted after.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the dyed turban is the whole seduction in one detail: foreign princes, dressed to impress, and a city that wanted to be like them.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
